subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but rich model: a jaguar-eagle alebrije hybrid with a quadruped jaguar body, eagle head and wings, and a feathered tail, painted in the bright, swirling, dotted patterns typical of carved wooden alebrijes.

Working out the skeleton structure now: hips joint, spine chain built from a few catmull points running from lower back to chest, then a neck chain curving up to the head, with a head joint oriented forward and a jaw joint following.

For the body mesh I'm planning a sweep along the spine with a tapering radius, then styling it in bold alebrije colors — gold-orange base with turquoise or magenta rosette spots and a cream-pink countershaded belly.

Writing sweep radius function...

For the neck I'm thinking of a feathered collar made from a ring of spike shapes radiating outward along the neck joint, colored alternately for an alebrije look, then moving to construct the eagle-style head with a skull sphere and separate upper and lower beak pieces.

For the beak itself I'm positioning a squashed cone shape at the head, tip pointing forward and slightly down, with the base tucked toward the back and a flattened horizontal scale to get that hooked-beak silhouette.

For the eyes I'm planning small circular decals with a concentric-color SVG texture placed symmetrically on either side of the head, giving the sense of pupil and iris without needing full sphere geometry.

Working out placement so the circle sits right on the skull's surface using the normal direction, and I'm about to add rounded ear spheres on top of the head for a jaguar-like silhouette.

Now I'm planning the limb structure: four legs with shoulder and hip joints, defining foot targets and segment lengths, and setting bend directions so the front elbows angle backward while checking that the hind leg reach doesn't exceed the total limb length.

Naming the joints along each chain, deciding which side gets the "L" suffix based on position, and attaching each leg chain to the appropriate spine or hip joint. Finally I'm adding sweeps for leg thickness with coat coloring and placing paw shapes at the chain tips.

Still writing paw details...

Now I'm planning the wing structure, defining shoulder-elbow-wrist joint chains spreading from the back, naming them with side suffixes and parenting them to the spine joints.

Working out the primary feather shapes as fan-arranged extrusions from the wrist, each with a tapered leaf-like outline...

I need the extrusion axes set so the feather lies flat horizontally rather than vertically -- using the outward direction as one axis and a forward vector as the other, keeping them non-parallel so the thickness comes out vertical.

Now I'm laying out the feather fan: computing direction vectors that sweep from outward toward backward, then arranging primaries at the wrist, secondaries along the elbow-to-wrist span, and coverts in layered rows with decreasing length. I want each feather to get a two-tone color gradient from base to tip, so I'm sketching a cheap paint function that switches color based on position along the feather's length.

I'm defining bone attachment points -- wrist for primaries, elbow for secondaries -- and sweeping the wing arm chain with tapering radii for the coat color. The wing sits around y~1.0 with roughly a 2m span, posed in a spread rest position. For the tail, I'm building a curved bone chain from the hips through three tail segments using catmull interpolation, then sweeping tapered radii with striped coloring along its length.

Now I'm working out the tail-tip feather fan: orienting each feather's extrusion plane so the thickness axis stays roughly vertical while the fan spreads in the horizontal plane, picking basis vectors carefully so they stay non-parallel. Then I move on to the body coat pattern, combining countershading with a spotted texture using a gold base and teal/magenta accent colors.

For the rosettes I'm choosing a brighter purple-black ring color against an orange base with teal and magenta accent dots, sized and spaced for an alebrije-style look, plus a cream-yellow countershaded belly. I'm also considering scattering small contrasting dot decorations along the spine using a surface-scatter approach with dozens of small sphere hits instead of a simple line sweep.

I want to add decal-based motifs too, like a swirling flower pattern placed near the flank surface and repeated on the wings, giving three or four texture types total (eye, flower, swirl). Then I'm working out the body's spine sweep geometry, defining how its radius tapers from hips to chest with rounded caps, and planning overlapping spheres at the chest and rump for a fuller silhouette.

Now I'm sketching the neck as a tapered sweep leading into the head sphere, adding small rounded jaguar-style ears with pink inner detail, and setting up a crest of spike-like feathers along the back of the head using a loop to place each base point.

Still writing crest geometry...

Still placing facial features...

Adding the hook-tip cone near the top of the beak, then checking overall body proportions—paws grounded near zero, head crest around 1.35, wings raised to about 1.05. Now I'm laying out the wing joint chain with root, elbow, and tip points for the catmull curve.

Still writing wing geometry...

Defining feather outline shape...

Still defining skeleton structure...

Adding helper functions, stick dots scattered along the body sweep, and flower decals placed on the flanks.

Adjusting the tilt to -45 so the ruff spikes angle backward and down rather than up, using two neck rings for a fuller collar effect. For the head, I'll keep the skull paint matching the coat pattern and skip adding separate eye-ring textures since the eye already handles that, then move toward finalizing colors and export.

Still assembling the model pieces...
